# Minimal DSP consumer of an installed Pulp SDK, plus its exclusion audit.
#
# This project is configured from OUTSIDE any Pulp source tree against a
# staged install prefix, which is the only vantage point where the question
# "what does adopting Pulp's DSP cost" has an honest answer. In-tree the answer
# is contaminated by options, aliases and BUILD_INTERFACE edges the consumer
# never sees.
#
# It MEASURES and REPORTS; it does not judge. The verdict belongs to the driver
# that knows the recorded state, and keeping the judgement out of here is what
# lets the executable still be built and symbol-audited on a branch where the
# contract is violated.

cmake_minimum_required(VERSION 3.24)
project(PulpCleanConsumerMinimal VERSION 0.1.0 LANGUAGES CXX)

if(NOT DEFINED PULP_CLEAN_CONSUMER_POLICY)
    message(FATAL_ERROR
        "PULP_CLEAN_CONSUMER_POLICY must point at exclusion_policy.cmake")
endif()
if(NOT DEFINED PULP_CLEAN_CONSUMER_CLOSURE_MODULE)
    message(FATAL_ERROR
        "PULP_CLEAN_CONSUMER_CLOSURE_MODULE must point at PulpConsumerClosure.cmake")
endif()
if(NOT DEFINED PULP_CLEAN_CONSUMER_REPORT)
    message(FATAL_ERROR "PULP_CLEAN_CONSUMER_REPORT must name the output file")
endif()

find_package(Pulp CONFIG REQUIRED COMPONENTS signal timebase)

foreach(_component signal timebase)
    if(NOT Pulp_${_component}_FOUND)
        message(FATAL_ERROR
            "Pulp did not report required component ${_component}")
    endif()
endforeach()

add_executable(pulp-clean-consumer-minimal main.cpp)
target_link_libraries(pulp-clean-consumer-minimal PRIVATE Pulp::signal Pulp::timebase)

# ── Audit ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

include("${PULP_CLEAN_CONSUMER_CLOSURE_MODULE}")
include("${PULP_CLEAN_CONSUMER_POLICY}")

# Measure the closure from the roots the consumer actually named. Reading the
# executable's own closure rather than the roots' would fold in the toolchain's
# implicit libraries, which are not Pulp's to answer for.
set(_roots Pulp::signal Pulp::timebase)
pulp_consumer_link_closure(_closure ${_roots})

set(_report "# Generated by the clean-consumer fixture. Do not edit.\n")
string(APPEND _report "set(PULP_CLEAN_CONSUMER_OBSERVED_CLOSURE\n")
foreach(_target IN LISTS _closure)
    string(APPEND _report "    ${_target}\n")
endforeach()
string(APPEND _report ")\n")

set(_violated "")
set(_unenforceable "")
set(_clean "")

foreach(_group IN LISTS PULP_CLEAN_CONSUMER_GROUPS)
    pulp_consumer_classify_exclusion("${_group}" _status _offenders
        CLOSURE ${_closure}
        REALIZED_BY ${PULP_CLEAN_CONSUMER_REALIZED_BY_${_group}})

    if(_status STREQUAL "violated")
        list(APPEND _violated "${_group}")
        string(APPEND _report
            "set(PULP_CLEAN_CONSUMER_OBSERVED_OFFENDERS_${_group}\n")
        foreach(_offender IN LISTS _offenders)
            string(APPEND _report "    ${_offender}\n")
        endforeach()
        string(APPEND _report ")\n")

        # Attribution, emitted as data rather than prose because the next
        # change acts on it. Three facts per offender, and each answers a
        # different question: WHICH module introduced the edge, HOW it holds
        # it (a declared interface dependency is a different fix from CMake's
        # own LINK_ONLY record of a PRIVATE static link), and the SHORTEST
        # route to it (the fewest edges anybody has to cut).
        foreach(_offender IN LISTS _offenders)
            string(MAKE_C_IDENTIFIER "${_offender}" _key)
            pulp_consumer_edge_carriers(_carriers "${_offender}"
                CLOSURE ${_closure})
            string(APPEND _report
                "set(PULP_CLEAN_CONSUMER_CARRIERS_${_key} ${_carriers})\n")

            set(_kinds "")
            foreach(_carrier IN LISTS _carriers)
                pulp_consumer_edge_kind(_kind "${_carrier}" "${_offender}")
                list(APPEND _kinds "${_carrier}:${_kind}")
            endforeach()
            string(APPEND _report
                "set(PULP_CLEAN_CONSUMER_EDGE_KIND_${_key} \"${_kinds}\")\n")

            foreach(_root ${_roots})
                pulp_consumer_shortest_path(_path "${_root}" "${_offender}")
                if(_path)
                    string(MAKE_C_IDENTIFIER "${_root}" _root_key)
                    string(APPEND _report
                        "set(PULP_CLEAN_CONSUMER_PATH_${_root_key}_${_key}"
                        " \"${_path}\")\n")
                endif()
            endforeach()
        endforeach()
    elseif(_status STREQUAL "unenforceable")
        list(APPEND _unenforceable "${_group}")
    else()
        list(APPEND _clean "${_group}")
    endif()
endforeach()

foreach(_bucket VIOLATED UNENFORCEABLE CLEAN)
    string(TOLOWER "${_bucket}" _lower)
    string(APPEND _report
        "set(PULP_CLEAN_CONSUMER_OBSERVED_${_bucket}_GROUPS ${_${_lower}})\n")
endforeach()

file(WRITE "${PULP_CLEAN_CONSUMER_REPORT}" "${_report}")

# Echo the same verdict into the configure log. The driver reads the file, but
# a human reading CI output should not have to go find it.
if(_violated)
    message(STATUS
        "clean-consumer: minimal DSP closure VIOLATES [${_violated}]")
else()
    message(STATUS "clean-consumer: minimal DSP closure violates nothing")
endif()
if(_unenforceable)
    message(STATUS
        "clean-consumer: NOT ENFORCEABLE against this SDK [${_unenforceable}]"
        " (no realizing target installed; these prove nothing here)")
endif()
